title: Randomized Trial of Therapy Alpha in Adults With Chronic Pruritus
content: In this synthetic 24-week randomized controlled trial, 240 adults with moderate-to-severe chronic pruritus received Therapy Alpha or placebo. At week 16, 45 percent of participants receiving Therapy Alpha achieved at least a four-point reduction in itch severity compared with 21 percent receiving placebo. Improvements were also observed in sleep interference. Common adverse events included headache, nasopharyngitis, and mild injection-site reactions. The trial duration limits conclusions about long-term safety.

title: Long-Term Extension Study of Therapy Alpha
content: This synthetic 52-week extension followed 180 adults previously enrolled in Therapy Alpha studies. Reductions in chronic pruritus were generally maintained through week 52. Injection-site reactions and headache remained the most frequently reported adverse events. No new common safety pattern was observed, but the sample size and duration were insufficient to characterize rare adverse events or safety beyond one year.

title: Therapy Beta for Adolescent Allergic Asthma
content: This synthetic study evaluated Therapy Beta in adolescents with allergic asthma. The study did not evaluate Therapy Alpha, adults with chronic pruritus, itch severity, or the safety profile relevant to the proposed Therapy Alpha use.
